sonnet.problem: Card 8 already asks about the altars in both courtyards (v5), and only then does card 9 tell v4, the altars in the LORD's house. That jumps ahead in verse order. Card 9 also re-tells the fact card 8 just revealed (altars in the LORD's house) as if it were new.
sonnet.rule: Cards follow the passage in order. A choice card can look back at a verse an earlier card in the same stop told, but never jumps ahead. / An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The card cites 33:3-5 but tells only the host of heaven (v3). It merely teases the altars of v4-5 without telling them, so the citation is wider than what the card tells.
sonnet.rule: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

sonnet.problem: Most of this card is the outside passage about Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 32:26). Only five words tell this passage ('Manasseh prays to the LORD'). The Hezekiah line also hints that humbling turns away wrath, which sets up the answer to card 4.
sonnet.rule: An outside passage, like a New Testament fulfillment, only rides along in a few words on a card that tells this passage. It never gets a card of its own, and a choice card never asks about it.

sonnet.problem: The right answer 'God' is a noun, while the wrong answers 'silent' and 'distant' are adjectives. The right answer stands out by its kind.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. / Don't let the right answer stand out.

sonnet.problem: The question says Amon did evil 'as his father Manasseh had done'. That hands over the answer ('All the idols his father Manasseh made') and rules out the wrong answers (Jeroboam's calves, Dagon). The question also packs v21-22 facts in with no story card.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it. / A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
